title: Borophene-Gold Nanohybrid Immunosensor for In Situ EV Lysis and Cancer Biomarker Detection by Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy.
authors: Praween N, Manoharan AT, Basu PK
abstract: Extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived biomarkers provide valuable molecular information for early cancer detection and disease monitoring, yet their analysis typically requires labor-intensive EV isolation and chemical lysis, limiting access and increasing assay complexity. Here, we present a label-free, non-faradaic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (nf-EIS) biosensor based on liquid-phase-exfoliated borophene (BP) integrated onto gold electrodes for direct detection of circulating and EV-derived biomarkers in serum. BP-Au interface provides an electrochemically active, high-capacitance sensing surface via interfacial charge transfer and orbital interactions, while electron-deficient boron sites enable direct coordination with glutaraldehyde and stable antibody immobilization without insulating linker layers. To improve biomarker accessibility, we investigated two reagent-free electric-field (EF) strategies: post-capture EV permeabilization and direct high-frequency (HF) EF treatment of serum. Direct HF EF treatment temporarily permeabilized EV membranes, quickly transporting biomarkers to the sensor, enhancing target capture and nf-EIS response. Compared to EV isolation, serum HF EF treatment reduced assay time to 45 min and improved biomarker recovery. The platform achieved limit of detection ranging from 0.02 to 0.57 pg/mL for five clinically relevant EV biomarkers (TSG101, GM2AP, MUC1, MUC5AC, and EGFR). Clinical evaluation of serum samples from healthy subjects (n = 20) and lung cancer patients (n = 20) showed improved sensing performance, increasing ROC-AUC values from 0.870-0.984 to 0.985-1.000 and sensitivity by up to 16.7% following HF EF-treatment. These findings demonstrate that integrating BP-enabled signal amplification with EF-assisted EV biomarker release provides a rapid, reagent-free, and isolation-free nf-EIS platform for sensitive, multiplexed liquid biopsy, with potential for early cancer detection and decentralized clinical diagnostics.

title: Identification of Prognostic Factors in Stage IV Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Multinational, Multicenter Real-World Project.
authors: Lee D, Serra MM, Hwang G et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in treatments, prognosis in stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains heterogeneous. Three studies conducted in South Korea, France and the United States (US) identified patient-, tumor-, and treatment-related factors across multiple therapy lines.
METHODS: All studies aimed to predict overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in stage IV NSCLC. The Korean study developed a machine learning (ML)-based prognostic model using a national retrospective observational cohort of patients treated at Samsung Medical Center. The US study analyzed 610 patients who had completed first-line therapy from the Cancer Outcomes Tracking and Analysis (COTA) NSCLC dataset, while the French study analyzed 263 patients from the Centre Léon Bérard receiving first-line treatment for NSCLC. Models were trained on 70% of patients and validated on the remaining 30%. Predictive performance was evaluated using C-index, gradient boosting, or receiver operating characteristic curves with calculation of area under the curve.
RESULTS: The Korean study analyzed 6,924 patients receiving first-line systemic therapy, representing 16,889 treatment-line instances up to eighth lines. C-index values for OS prediction were 0.748 (CoxPH), 0.746 (RSf), and 0.735 (gradient boosting); for PFS, they were 0.724, 0.720, and 0.716, respectively. Favorable prognostic factors included female sex, higher body mass index (BMI), EGFR/ALK/ROS1 alterations, PD-L1 positivity, adenocarcinoma histology, preserved hematologic and nutritional markers, current targeted therapy, and longer prior treatment duration. Poor prognosis was associated with higher ECOG status, advanced therapy line, shorter prior treatment duration, liver or bone metastasis, leptomeningeal disease, PIK3CA mutation, and elevated inflammatory or hepatic markers. Some predictors were consistent across countries while others were country specific. In the US cohort, higher albumin and creatinine levels, female sex, longer treatment duration, longer time since diagnosis, higher BMI, and less extensive metastatic disease predicted improved OS and/or PFS. French cohort analyses identified higher hemoglobin and creatinine levels, absence of MET alteration, and adenocarcinoma histology as predictors of improved PFS.
CONCLUSION: The Korean ML-based prognostic model showed robust predictive performance across multiple therapy lines and may support individualized risk stratification and treatment planning by identifying patients with higher risk of poor prognosis. Differences observed across international cohorts highlight the importance of incorporating geographic variability into prognostic models to improve their clinical applicability and inform region-specific treatment decision-making.

title: Prognostic role of macrophage phenotypes, spatial distribution and differential iNOS expression in NSCLC.
authors: Brinker G, Franzen K, Drömann D et al.
abstract: The immune microenvironment has been shown to significantly impact the prognosis of various tumor entities. Spatial immunophenotyping has emerged as a promising technique to characterize the tumor microenvironment and explore new biomarkers aiding in prognostic evaluation. In this study, we aimed to elaborate further on the prognostic role of macrophages in the microenvironment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). For that purpose, we performed multiplex immunofluorescence on a large binational cohort, dividing the macrophage phenotype spectrum into CD68+CD163-iNOS- macrophage-like, M1-like, M1M2-like, and M2-like phenotype. Quantitatively, we observed the CD68+CD163-iNOS- population to be the most abundant subset. High M1-like and CD68+CD163-iNOS- densities seemed to confer a better prognosis, whereas M1M2-like seemed unfavorable in this context. In line with this, the combination of low CD68+CD163-iNOS- and low M1-like cell counts showed a significantly worse outcome than other combinations. Interestingly, semi-quantitative expression analysis revealed that iNOS expression in intratumoral macrophages, which in our study characterized M1-like polarization, correlated inversely with prognosis. In multivariate nearest neighbor analysis, we demonstrated that short tumor-to-M1-like distances, as well as short tumor-to-CD68+CD163-iNOS- distances, seemed to convey a generally better prognosis independent of age, sex and stage. Again, the combination of these markers seemed to strengthen this effect. Various immune-to-immune cell distances also showed a strong impact on prognosis. On a molecular level, we did not appreciate any impact of KRAS and EGFR status on macrophage density or spatial configuration between different macrophage phenotypes. We did, however, observe a varied effect on tumor cell-immune cell proximity in KRAS and EGFR mutated tumors. Hence, our data put forward a complex, yet prognostically important role for macrophages in NSCLC microenvironment. Our data further validate the important role of macrophages in the microenvironment of NSCLC and suggest candidate biomarkers for prognostic estimation.

title: Diagnosis of leptomeningeal metastasis with concurrent tuberculous meningitis assisted by cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing combined with copy number variation analysis: a case report.
authors: Zhang T, Xiong X, Zhang M et al.
abstract: Concurrent tuberculous meningitis (TBM) and leptomeningeal metastasis from lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD-LM) are exceptionally rare and pose significant diagnostic challenges. Overlapping clinical and neuroimaging features often lead to misdiagnosis or diagnostic delay. Here, we report a 69-year-old woman with a prior history of bilateral invasive lung adenocarcinoma lesions who had undergone surgical resection. Although genetic testing identified an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation, targeted therapy was not initiated at that time. Two weeks before admission, the patient developed progressive dizziness and headache, which rapidly evolved into cognitive impairment and intractable projectile vomiting. Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed hydrocephalus and diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology demonstrated atypical cells, initially suggesting LUAD-LM. However, metagenomic next-generation sequencing combined with copy number variation analysis (mNGS-CNV) of the CSF detected both multiple chromosomal copy number alterations and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These findings supported the concurrent diagnoses of LUAD-LM and TBM. The patient was treated with EGFR-targeted therapy in combination with a four-drug anti-tuberculosis regimen. At one-year follow-up, her condition remained stable. This case highlights the potential value of CSF mNGS-CNV in recognizing concurrent infectious and neoplastic meningeal diseases from a single CSF specimen.

title: Machine-Learning-Guided Identification of Potent Osimertinib Analogues Targeting the EGFR Triple Mutant.
authors: Ahamad S, Kuldeep J, Ahmad S et al.
abstract: Background: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations, including exon 19 deletions and L858R, are major drivers of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although osimertinib is an established EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), the emergence of T790M and C797S mutations can reduce its effectiveness. This study aimed to identify and computationally prioritize osimertinib analogues with potential activity against the EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S triple mutant using an integrated machine-learning-assisted cheminformatics and structure-based approach. Methods: A library of 297,420 osimertinib analogues retrieved from PubChem was represented using physicochemical descriptors and 2048-bit Morgan fingerprints. Principal component analysis, t-SNE, UMAP, K-means clustering, and HDBSCAN were used to characterize chemical space, while Tanimoto similarity and Isolation Forest analysis were applied to assess structural similarity and scaffold novelty. Shortlisted compounds were subsequently evaluated using Glide extra-precision (XP) docking, induced-fit docking (IFD), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Results: K-means analysis identified an osimertinib-containing cluster comprising 17,149 compounds, providing a focused chemical space for analogue prioritization. A clear inverse relationship was observed between Tanimoto similarity to osimertinib and quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) among the top 30 compounds (Pearson's r = -0.86). Three compounds satisfied the predefined combination of Tanimoto similarity ≥ 0.4 and QED ≥ 0.5. Subsequent molecular modelling highlighted compounds 155515815 and 122474632, together with osimertinib, as compounds exhibiting favorable and stable interactions with key EGFR residues. MD simulations further supported the stability of the protein-ligand complexes, while DFT analysis provided additional insight into their electronic and molecular properties. Conclusions: The integrated machine-learning-assisted and structure-based workflow enabled systematic exploration of a large osimertinib analogue library and identified computationally prioritized candidates for further investigation against the EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S triple mutant. Compounds 155515815 and 122474632 showed favorable computational profiles across multiple analyses and may serve as starting points for further scaffold optimization. Experimental studies are required to determine their biological activity and potential to address osimertinib resistance.

title: Mucosal, Ocular, and Pulmonary Adverse Events Reported with Datopotamab Deruxtecan: An Indication-Restricted Disproportionality Analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System.
authors: Kaya OB, Karabuğa B, Aydemir E et al.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Datopotamab deruxtecan was approved in 2025 for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); its safety profile in routine use has not been described. We characterized adverse event reporting for the agent and asked whether the events reported most disproportionately are those that carry the reported harm. Methods: Reports naming datopotamab deruxtecan as a primary suspect in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS, 2025Q1-2026Q1) were stratified by recorded indication and compared with all other reports recording the same indication. A signal required at least three reports and pre-specified frequentist (reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio, chi-square), Bayesian (lower credibility bound of the information component, IC025), and multiplicity-adjusted thresholds. Sacituzumab govitecan served as a within-class comparator, reference pools were pruned of agents causing the same event, and outcomes were recalculated after excluding reports coding disease progression. Results: Among 416 reports (196 breast, 118 NSCLC), mucosal and ocular events dominated: the ROR for stomatitis was 21.50 (95% CI: 15.04-30.74) and 17.72 (9.93-31.63), with keratitis, oral candidiasis, and dry eye also qualifying. Against sacituzumab govitecan, stomatitis persisted (19.75), while myelosuppressive and gastrointestinal terms were markedly less reported. Interstitial lung disease met the Evans criteria but not the Bayesian or multiplicity threshold in the breast stratum (2.51), and did not meet any criterion in the lung stratum (2.09) or against the comparator; the reports carrying it nevertheless recorded the heaviest harm, with eighteen out of nineteen being serious (94.7%, 95% CI: 74.0-99.9) and five out of nineteen being fatal (26.3%, 95% CI: 9.1-51.2), while no fatal outcome remained among the 66 progression-free mucosal reports. Trastuzumab deruxtecan supplied 30.3% of pulmonary reports in the breast reference pool; removing it raised the estimate to 3.70 with an IC025 of 0.41. Conclusions: Reporting for datopotamab deruxtecan is dominated by mucosal and ocular toxicity, whereas interstitial lung disease is reported less often but in reports recording a far higher proportion of serious and fatal outcomes. Its absence from the primary signal lists reflects a comparison base containing agents that cause the same event rather than an absence of risk, and monitoring intensity should not follow the magnitude of disproportionality. Spontaneous reports are subject to under-reporting, stimulated reporting, and incomplete data, and disproportionality describes patterns of reporting rather than incidence or risk.

title: Lipid Metabolic Rewiring in Cancer Drug Resistance: Pathways, Networks, and Therapeutic Strategies.
authors: Chang SN, Raggi C, Exil V
abstract: Drug resistance limits cancer therapy, and metabolic reprogramming helps tumor cells adapt to therapeutic stress. This review examines how altered lipid uptake, synthesis, storage, and oxidation support survival by changing signaling, membrane composition, energy production, redox balance, and tumor-microenvironment interactions. The SCAP/SREBP axis is a key transcriptional regulator; oncogenic and nutrient signaling (EGFR, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, mutant p53) controls SREBP abundance and activation, and sustained SREBP activity during treatment distinguishes resistant from sensitive cells in several models, including gefitinib-resistant lung cancer and sorafenib/lenvatinib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). MicroRNAs regulate these pathways post-transcriptionally, including ferroptosis-related targets (ACSL4, SLC7A11, GPX4). Inhibitors of lipogenesis, SCAP/SREBP, cholesterol metabolism, fatty-acid oxidation, lipid uptake and storage, phospholipid and sphingolipid signaling, and ferroptosis have improved drug sensitivity in preclinical models. However, many studies show only an association with resistance rather than that modulating a pathway restores sensitivity; findings vary between tumor types; and compensatory rewiring, toxicity, and limited tumor selectivity constrain single-target approaches, while miRNA-based therapeutics remain early-stage. Rational combinations guided by lipidomic and transcriptomic profiling are a priority.

title: Association Between Severe Vitamin D Deficiency and 5-Year Healthcare Utilization and Mortality in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Cohort Study.
authors: Chiang JK, Kao HH, Chiang PH et al.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a common malignancy and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Vitamin D supplementation may improve survival in patients with early stage NSCLC and low serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels. Using real-world data from the TriNetX research platform, this study aimed to examine the associations between baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentrations and the risks of all-cause mortality, first hospitalization, first emergency department (ED) visit, and first intensive care unit (ICU) admission among adults with NSCLC. Materials and Methods: A retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX database was conducted to investigate the relationship between vitamin D deficiency and patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults (≥20 years). Patients were stratified into four groups according to serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels: Group A (≤10 ng/mL; severe vitamin D deficiency), Group B (>10 to 20 ng/mL), Group C (>20 to 30 ng/mL), and Group D (>30 to 100 ng/mL; normal vitamin D status). To minimize exposure misclassification, all patients required a confirmatory serum 25(OH)D measurement within 3 months before the index date. After 1:1 propensity score matching, patients were followed for up to 5 years to assess the predefined clinical outcomes. Results: A total of 4794 eligible patients with NSCLC were included and stratified into four groups: Group A (n = 738; 15.4%), Group B (n = 1204; 25.1%), Group C (n = 1237; 25.8%), and Group D (n = 1615; 33.7%). After propensity score matching, baseline characteristics were generally well balanced across the vitamin D groups, with only minor residual imbalances in eGFR and serum albumin. After propensity score matching, patients with severe vitamin D deficiency (Group A) consistently had a higher risk of all-cause mortality at 1, 3, and 5 years than those in Groups B, C, or D (all p < 0.05). Group A also showed higher risks of 1-year first ED visits, malnutrition, and bone metastasis in selected comparisons, and higher risks of first ED visits throughout follow-up when compared with Group D. Conclusions: In this real-world analysis of patients with NSCLC, severe vitamin D deficiency at baseline was consistently associated with higher all-cause mortality than all other baseline vitamin D categories over 5 years. Associations with first hospitalization, ED visit, and ICU admission were less consistent and were most evident in comparison with study-defined normal vitamin D status, particularly for first ED visit. However, low serum 25(OH)D levels may primarily reflect overall clinical vulnerability, and their independent prognostic value remains uncertain.

title: EGFR-Mutated Small Cell Lung Cancer: Molecular Characterization and Clinical Implications of EGFR-TKIs.
authors: Ampazis D, Bosgana P, Pavli E et al.
abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy defined by a number of genetic and molecular features, including near-universal TP53 and RB1 inactivation, MYC amplifications, Notch pathway disruption, and hyperactivated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. The subtypes of SCLC, SCLC-A/N/P/I, are primarily based on four transcription regulators (ASCL1, NeuroD1, YAP1, POU). This review provides a concise overview of the molecular landscape of SCLC and then focuses on the subset displaying epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) alterations. EGFR-positive SCLC presents either as rare primary (de novo) disease (2.6-19.3%) or as transformed SCLC originating from EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in 3-14% of cases following EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. In both cases, the tumors harbor EGFR mutations with the most frequent one being exon 19 deletions. A number of pathways have been identified regarding the lineage transformation with the co-occurring TP53 and RB1 loss predominating, while a number of other molecular mechanisms have been explored, including activation of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition factors (ZEB1, SLUG), MDM4 or BCL2L2/NFKBIA co-amplifications, and newly postulated genetic variants such as FBN1 and PALLD, alongside emergent surface expression of DLL3, B7-H3, and PTK7. Once SCLC transformation occurs, tumors tend to drop EGFR dependence and display profound resistance to EGFR-TKIs, necessitating a shift to standard platinum-etoposide chemotherapy, with or without immunotherapy. The value of EGFR-TKIs has been explored, as an add-on treatment, in several cases and its efficacy has not so far provided satisfactory outcomes. An update of the literature, within this particular field, is being provided along with the value for routine serial re-biopsy (tissue or liquid) upon disease progression, especially when EGFR-TKIs have been used. Early identification of neuroendocrine transformation can prevent futile EGFR-TKI monotherapy, capture mixed histologies, and recognize potential re-transformation back to adenocarcinoma.

title: CCND2 Expression in Lung Adenocarcinoma and Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Prognostic and Transcriptomic Associations in TCGA and GEO Cohorts.
authors: Jeong U, An JH, Park NH et al.
abstract: CCND2 has context-dependent roles in cancer, but its prognostic relevance in the major histological subtypes of non-small cell lung cancer remains uncertain. We evaluated CCND2 separately in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) using The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)data from OncoLnc and the Genomic Data Commons, together with three independent Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) cohorts. Continuous-expression overall survival (OS) models were prespecified as the principal survival analyses. In matched tumor-normal pairs, CCND2 expression was lower in LUAD tumors (p < 0.001), with a nonsignificant difference in LUSC (p = 0.054). In TCGA-LUAD, higher CCND2 expression was associated with a lower mortality hazard after clinical adjustment (HR per SD = 0.839, 95% CI 0.722-0.975, p = 0.022; 0.841 without the pack-years-recorded indicator), with similar estimates in detailed-stage, EGFR-adjusted, and purity-adjusted models. The LUSC association was nonsignificant (HR = 0.888, 95% CI 0.776-1.017, p = 0.085), and a formal histology interaction test was nonsignificant (p = 0.235). Adding CCND2 to clinical models yielded only a small, uncertain gain in the C-index. External associations were heterogeneous and partly probe-dependent, and pooled estimates were nonsignificant in both histologies. Gene correlations were small, and pathway enrichments described bulk-tissue association patterns. CCND2 is an exploratory prognostic candidate in LUAD that requires further validation before clinical application.

title: Lung Cancer in Non-Smokers as a Distinct Disease: A Literature Review.
authors: Cieślik-Wolski B, Smolarz B, Romanowicz H et al.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, traditionally attributed to tobacco smoking. However, lung cancer in non-smokers (LCINS) is increasingly recognized as a distinct clinical and biological entity, currently affecting an estimated 350,000-625,000 individuals globally. This narrative review synthesizes recent literature on the epidemiology, etiology, and management of LCINS. We examine the contributions of sex, ethnicity, environmental pollutants (particulate matter, radon, cooking oil vapors, second-hand smoke), and comorbid lung diseases to LCINS risk. Molecular profiling reveals a landscape dominated by targetable driver alterations, including EGFR, ALK, or other supporting mutations in genes ROS1, RET, KRAS, TP53, and HER2, along with distinct mutational signatures and evolutionary trajectories compared with smoking-related tumors. We further discuss emerging diagnostic strategies and therapeutic approaches, including targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors or immune checkpoint inhibitors. Our findings support classifying LCINS as a biologically distinct subtype of lung cancer rather than simply lung cancer in the absence of tobacco exposure, with implications for screening criteria and personalized treatment strategies. Further research is needed to clarify its multifactorial origins.

title: Clinical-to-Pathological Nodal Discordance and Postoperative Outcomes by EGFR Mutation Subtype in Resected Clinically Node-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
authors: Manabe T, Takenaka M, Okawara M et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Clinical nodal classification may differ from postoperative pathological findings in lung cancer. We evaluated nodal discordance and mutation-specific outcomes in surgically treated, clinically node-positive epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with clinical N1-2, stage II-III disease treated at four Japanese institutions from 2012 to 2020. EGFR exon 19 deletion (Del19) and exon 21 L858R point mutation (L858R) were compared in exploratory postoperative and post-recurrence survival analyses.
RESULTS: Among 66 patients, 33 had Del19, 28 had L858R, and 5 had uncommon mutations; 52 underwent upfront surgery and 14 received preoperative treatment. Among 42 patients with clinical N1 disease, 18 (42.9%) had postoperative pathological N2 disease. The adjusted hazard ratio for postoperative overall survival with L858R versus Del19 was 1.99 (95% confidence interval, 0.97-4.09); the corresponding progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0.99 (0.54-1.81). In the pooled pathological common-mutation cohort, post-recurrence overall survival was evaluated in 33 patients with 25 deaths (univariable hazard ratio, 1.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.64-3.11; log-rank p = 0.388). Post-recurrence progression-free survival was evaluated in 26 patients and favored Del19 in an unadjusted comparison (log-rank p = 0.023).
CONCLUSIONS: Nodal discordance was frequent in this selected surgical population. The imprecise survival estimates establish neither equivalent prognosis nor an independent adverse effect of L858R. Post-recurrence findings require external validation with treatment-adjusted analyses.

title: First-Line Treatment of EGFR-Mutated Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Osimertinib, Osimertinib Plus Chemotherapy, and Amivantamab Plus Lazertinib with Focus on Efficacy, Safety, Acquired Resistance, and Health-Economic Considerations.
authors: Shrem NS, Soklakova A, Meirovitz A et al.
abstract: Background: Treatment of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved from first-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) to third-generation osimertinib and, more recently, to intensified first-line regimens. Osimertinib monotherapy remains effective and comparatively tolerable, while osimertinib plus platinum-pemetrexed and amivantamab plus lazertinib improve progression-free and overall survival at the cost of greater toxicity. This article evaluates current first- and subsequent-line treatment strategies for advanced NSCLC harboring common sensitizing EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R substitutions), with particular attention to efficacy, toxicity, resistance mechanisms, and patient selection. Methods: A structured assessment of phase III randomized trials, published network meta-analyses and indirect comparisons, and resistance-focused literature was conducted to compare efficacy, toxicity, resistance mechanisms, costs, and patient-selection considerations across current treatments. No original statistical analysis was performed; comparative estimates were derived from published studies. Results: First-line intensification with osimertinib plus chemotherapy or amivantamab plus lazertinib improves progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) over osimertinib alone in EGFR-mutant NSCLC, particularly in high-risk patients, but it also increases toxicity, and resistance remains heterogeneous and may require repeat molecular profiling to guide further therapy. Published indirect comparisons have not shown a significant difference between the two intensified regimens. Conclusions: No single regimen suits all patients. Fit patients with high-risk features may derive the greatest absolute benefit from first-line intensification. Apparent differences between osimertinib plus platinum-pemetrexed and amivantamab plus lazertinib in subgroups (such as L858R or TP53 co-mutation) are based mainly on exploratory cross-trial data and do not establish superiority of either regimen. Amivantamab plus lazertinib offers a chemotherapy-free alternative with a distinct toxicity profile. Osimertinib monotherapy remains appropriate for patients with lower-risk disease, frailty, poorer performance status, or significant comorbidities, or for those who prefer a lower treatment burden; age alone should not determine treatment choice. Post-progression therapy should be guided by repeat biopsy, plasma genotyping, and identified resistance mechanisms.

title: Targeted Therapies for EGFR Exon 20 Insertion Mutations in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
authors: Cheng J, Wang K, Arter ZL et al.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations are among the most common oncogenic drivers in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with L858R point mutation or exon 19 deletions accounting for the majority of EGFR mutations. The development of EGFR-targeted therapies has significantly improved clinical outcomes and overall survival in patients harboring these classical activating mutations. However, EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (Ex20ins) exhibit resistance to earlier-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), including erlotinib, gefitinib, and afatinib, due to structural alterations that limit drug binding and reduce therapeutic efficacy. To address these challenges, novel EGFR-targeted TKIs and bispecific monoclonal antibodies have emerged as promising treatment strategies for patients with Ex20ins-mutated NSCLC. This review summarizes recent advances in targeted therapies for EGFR Ex20ins, highlighting treatments approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), including amivantamab and sunvozertinib, as well as emerging agents such as firmonertinib, zipalertinib, and becotarug.

title: Nuclear S100A4-HMGB1 promotes SLC7A11-dependent redox adaptation and ferroptosis tolerance in acquired osimertinib resistance.
authors: Guo H, Tang Q, Qin Y et al.
abstract: Acquired resistance limits the durable efficacy of osimertinib in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the redox adaptations that enable resistant cells to evade ferroptosis remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify nuclear S100A4 as a stress-responsive regulator of SLC7A11-dependent antioxidant defense during acquired osimertinib resistance. Osimertinib induces S100A4 through SP1-dependent transcriptional activation. S100A4 loss impairs cystine uptake and glutathione homeostasis, increases lipid peroxidation, and sensitizes cells to osimertinib, whereas its overexpression promotes resistance. Acute S100A4 depletion in independently generated resistant cells similarly increases lipid-peroxidative stress, reduces SLC7A11 expression, and restores osimertinib sensitivity. Ferroptosis inhibition substantially attenuates the sensitization caused by S100A4 loss, supporting ferroptosis as a functionally important component of S100A4-mediated resistance. Mechanistically, nuclear S100A4 interact with HMGB1 within an SLC7A11 promoter-associated chromatin complex, supporting SLC7A11 transcription. HMGB1 depletion impairs S100A4 occupancy at the SLC7A11 promoter, while S100A4 interaction-surface mutants reduce HMGB1 interaction and drug resistance. This regulatory program functionally converges with NRF2/ATF4 signaling, and SLC7A11 silencing attenuates S100A4-mediated osimertinib resistance. Paired pretreatment and post-progression specimens show coordinated increases in nuclear S100A4 and SLC7A11 following acquired EGFR-TKI resistance. Moreover, niclosamide increases ferroptotic stress and enhances osimertinib efficacy in resistant models, with genetic analyses indicating that S100A4 contributes to this sensitizing effect. Collectively, these findings identify a nuclear S100A4-HMGB1-SLC7A11 redox-adaptation program that contributes to ferroptosis tolerance and provides a rationale for exploiting redox vulnerabilities in osimertinib-resistant NSCLC.

title: Efficacy and safety of traditional Chinese medicine injections plus PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
authors: Hu X, Zhang Q, Sun J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, and most patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are diagnosed with advanced disease. Programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors combined with chemotherapy have become a standard first-line strategy, but primary or acquired resistance and immune-related adverse events limit durable benefit. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) injections are widely used as adjunctive therapy in China; however, their comparative efficacy and safety when added to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based treatment remain uncertain. This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) compared six commonly used TCM injections in this clinical setting.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science Core Collection, the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, the VIP Chinese Science and Technology Periodical Database and SinoMed were searched from inception to 9 July 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing a TCM injection plus the same PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based background regimen vs. that background regimen alone were eligible. Two investigators independently selected studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool version 1 (RoB 1). A frequentist NMA was performed in R 4.5.0 using netmeta 3.2-0. Binary outcomes were expressed as ORs and continuous outcomes as standardized mean differences (SMDs), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). All outcomes were analysed using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; SUCRA was calculated to describe the probability of favorable ranking but was not used as proof of superiority. The review was reported according to PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA.
RESULTS: Twelve RCTs involving 1,031 patients were included. Six injections were evaluated: Aidi injection (AD), Fufang Kushen injection (FFKS), Shenqi Fuzheng injection (SQFZ), Astragalus polysaccharide injection (HQDT), Shenmai injection (SM) and ginseng polysaccharide injection (RRDT). All graded comparisons were of low or very low certainty. Relative to the trial-specific control condition (CT), the ORs suggested higher objective response rates for FFKS (OR = 3.08, 95% CI 1.81-5.23), AD (OR = 2.93, 95% CI 1.55-5.55), SM (OR = 2.96, 95% CI 1.20-7.27), SQFZ (OR = 2.63, 95% CI 1.30-5.35) and RRDT (OR = 2.35, 95% CI 1.07-5.15); HQDT showed a non-significant association (OR = 2.34, 95% CI 0.98-5.56). FFKS, AD and SQFZ also had ORs above 1 for disease control. However, none of the pairwise comparisons among TCM injections was statistically significant. FFKS had the highest exploratory SUCRA value for ORR, but this ranking does not establish superiority. Low-certainty or very-low-certainty associations were also observed for selected immunological, quality-of-life and toxicity outcomes. The robustness of the total adverse-event estimate for FFKS varied with the continuity correction used.
CONCLUSION: The current evidence is insufficient to establish comparative efficacy or safety among TCM injections in patients receiving PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor-based therapy. The available estimates are based largely on small, open-label trials with heterogeneous background regimens, indirect comparisons and low or very low certainty. The observed associations require confirmation and should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence for selecting a particular injection.

title: Folate receptor α as a therapeutic target in cancer: molecular mechanisms, receptor-mediated drug delivery, and translational advances.
authors: Bodagala SR, Samathoti P
abstract: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) is a high-affinity folate-binding glycoprotein that is overexpressed in several epithelial cancers, including ovarian, triple-negative breast, mesothelioma, and non-small cell lung cancers, while exhibiting limited expression in normal tissues. Its selective expression and receptor-mediated endocytosis make FRα an attractive target for precision cancer therapy. This review summarizes the structure, biological functions, and oncogenic role of FRα, highlighting its involvement in tumor progression and signaling pathways. Recent advances in FRα-targeted therapeutics are discussed, including folic acid-functionalized nanoparticles and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). Folate-targeted liposomes, polymeric, silica-based, and metallic nanoparticles have demonstrated enhanced tumor targeting, cellular uptake, and anticancer efficacy in preclinical studies. In parallel, FRα-targeted ADCs, particularly the FDA-approved mirvetuximab soravtansine (Elahere®), along with emerging candidates such as MORAb-202 and STRO-002, have shown promising clinical outcomes. Despite these advances, challenges including receptor heterogeneity, off-target uptake, and drug resistance remain. Continued optimization of targeting strategies, nanocarrier design, and patient selection is expected to further improve the efficacy and safety of FRα-directed cancer therapies.

title: Prognostic Factors and Treatment Effect Modifier Candidates in Advanced HER2-Mutant NSCLC: A Targeted Literature Review.
authors: Lewis-Mikhael AM, Wang X, Bernard-Gauthier V et al.
abstract: Background: The expanding availability of targeted therapies for HER2-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has led to increased interest in understanding the baseline characteristics of patients that may impact clinical outcomes. This literature review evaluates prognostic factors and treatment effect modifiers in HER2-mutant NSCLC to inform indirect treatment comparison (ITC). Methods: A targeted literature review (TLR) was conducted and reported in accordance with an adapted PRISMA framework. The review included observational studies and clinical trials assessing survival outcomes among adults with advanced HER2-mutant NSCLC, irrespective of prior systemic therapy. Subgroups of interest included age, sex, smoking status, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS), metastatic status, prior treatment history, HER2-mutation subtype, and other clinically relevant baseline characteristics. Searches were conducted in Embase and MEDLINE to identify English-language publications from January 2019 to 20 December 2025. Results: Based on data from 33 included publications (19 observational studies and 14 publications reporting results from 11 clinical trials), most demographic factors, including age, sex, and smoking status, were not found to be of consistent prognostic or predictive value in HER2-mutant NSCLC patients. However, ECOG PS and metastatic burden showed the most consistent prognostic associations with clinical outcomes, whereas associations for HER2-mutation subtype (especially the YVMA/Y772_A775dup variant) were heterogeneous, appeared to differ by treatment and were largely exploratory. TP53 co-mutations were associated with poorer outcomes in all TKI-treated cohorts reporting them; no evidence is available for other treatment classes. Conclusions: These findings provide a structured evidence base for variable selection and sensitivity analyses in ITCs, while underscoring the need for prospective controlled studies capable of formally evaluating treatment heterogeneity in this molecularly distinct population.

title: Immunotherapy Resistance in Small Cell Lung Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities.
authors: Xu L, Cheng Y, Chen H et al.
abstract: In small cell lung cancer (SCLC), immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) combined with platinum-based chemotherapy are standard first-line treatment for extensive-stage disease. However, durable disease control remains uncommon. This review examines lineage plasticity, epigenetic regulation, defective antigen presentation, and altered DNA sensing and interferon responses. These processes interact with T-cell dysfunction, suppressive myeloid populations, and organ-specific niches. Treatment-associated clonal and cell-state changes complicate the distinction between chemotherapy resistance and immune escape. We relate these processes to primary and acquired resistance and assess interventions according to treatment setting and evidence source. Randomized SCLC trials support selected maintenance and first-line combination regimens and delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3)-directed T-cell redirection. By contrast, evidence for epigenetic, innate-immune, and myeloid targeting remains largely preclinical. Findings from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other tumors provide indirect evidence that cannot be extrapolated directly to SCLC. Emerging lineage vulnerabilities and traditional Chinese medicine remain exploratory. We discuss the overlap between chemotherapy and immunotherapy resistance, opportunities and constraints arising from plasticity, and the validation needed for mechanism-informed interventions.

title: From digital pathology to integrated precision oncology: AI-driven biomarker assessment and multimodal data integration in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Ilié M, Hofman P
abstract: Digital pathology (DP) is evolving from an image-based diagnostic modality into a quantitative platform for computational precision oncology. This transition is particularly relevant in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), where limited tissue specimens must support histological classification, immunohistochemistry, broad molecular profiling and an expanding range of therapy-linked biomarkers. Artificial intelligence (AI) can assist conventional tasks such as tissue segmentation, cell detection, quality control and biomarker quantification, but it can also derive image-based signatures associated with molecular alterations, spatial immune organization and treatment response. This review focuses primarily on NSCLC and examines the continuum from foundational image-analysis tasks and AI-assisted PD-L1 scoring to histology-based molecular prediction, computational companion diagnostics, pathology foundation models and multimodal AI. We discuss recent lung-specific evidence, including computational triage of actionable alterations, the emerging TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring paradigm and selected protein biomarkers associated with antibody-drug conjugates. We also consider the integration of pathology with genomics, transcriptomics, liquid biopsy, radiology and longitudinal clinical data. Particular attention is given to the barriers separating algorithmic performance from clinical utility: uneven adoption of whole-slide imaging, pre-analytical and scanner variability, missing or asynchronous multimodal data, propagation of upstream measurement errors, laboratory information-system interoperability, prospective validation, regulation, reimbursement and equitable access. Emerging paradigms such as digital twins and agentic AI are discussed as research directions rather than established clinical tools. We argue that the principal value of AI in NSCLC will not be autonomous diagnosis, but the reliable conversion of fragmented data streams into transparent, auditable and clinically actionable patient representations.

title: Endobronchial Ultrasound-Guided Transbronchial Needle Aspiration and Transbronchial Biopsy for Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions in Patients with Interstitial Lung Disease: A Phase Ⅱ Prospective Study.
authors: Ito T, Nishida K, Baba T et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The addition of radial endobronchial ultrasound (r-EBUS)-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA) to transbronchial biopsy (TBB) may improve the relationship between the r-EBUS probe and target lesion, helping overcome the limited efficacy of TBB alone. However, the efficacy and safety of this sequential procedure for peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain unknown. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance and safety of r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB for PPLs in patients with ILD.
METHODS: In a single-center, single-arm, phase Ⅱ trial, patients with PPLs and concomitant ILD were prospectively enrolled to undergo r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB under virtual bronchoscopy navigation and fluoroscopy. The primary endpoint was the diagnostic yield for PPLs. Secondary outcomes included improvement in r-EBUS findings, procedural time, and safety.
RESULTS: Forty-seven patients were analyzed, excluding one patient who was found to have an endobronchial lesion during bronchoscopy. The median maximum lesion diameter on computed tomography was 22.3 mm (range: 11.2-70.3 mm). The diagnostic yield for PPLs in patients with ILD was 78.7% (37/47 patients, lower 95% confidence interval: 66.6%, P < 0.001). Improvement in r-EBUS findings during TBNA/TBB procedures was observed in 70.8% (17/24 patients, 95% confidence interval: 48.9-87.4%). The median procedural time was approximately 50 min. Pneumothorax occurred in two patients, one of whom required thoracic drainage.
CONCLUSION: This phase II study suggested that sequential r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB might be a useful diagnostic approach for PPLs in patients with ILD, with no serious adverse events observed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: jRCT1042230076.

title: Interventional Oncology for Small Liver, Kidney, and Lung Tumors: Current Evidence and Emerging Treatment Strategies.
authors: Lanza C, D'Argenzio J, Pozzi J et al.
abstract: Image-guided ablation can treat small tumors while limiting tissue loss, but its clinical value also depends on the burden imposed on patients. This critical narrative review examines imaging, treatment selection, comparative outcomes, and follow-up for liver, renal, and lung tumors. A PubMed search, citation tracking, and targeted guideline and primary-study checks informed a nonexhaustive synthesis. Randomized evidence supports ablation in defined hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal liver metastasis populations, subject to trial eligibility and stopping rules. Renal and pulmonary comparisons remain predominantly observational; partial nephrectomy, contemporary lung-sparing surgery, surveillance, and stereotactic radiotherapy provide distinct alternatives. Tumor biology, achievable margins, adjacent structures, functional reserve, competing mortality, and patient preferences are more informative than diameter alone. Protective maneuvers can improve access in selected anatomically difficult cases. Hepatic irreversible electroporation and histotripsy broaden technical possibilities, but their oncological evidence and safety constraints require careful interpretation. Technical success, follow-up efficacy, retreatment, survival, and functional outcomes must be reported separately. Prospective comparisons should measure durable cancer control alongside anesthesia, hospital use, recovery, quality of life, and cumulative treatment burden. Treatment selection should integrate these outcomes through shared decision-making.

title: The Impact of Prehabilitation on Cognitive Function and Fatigue in Lung Cancer Patients Undergoing Surgical Treatment: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
authors: Mania K, Pieczyńska A, Hojan K
abstract: Background/Objectives: Surgical treatment for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) presents risks of cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) and postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD), which are further exacerbated by cancer-related fatigue. While multimodal prehabilitation improves physical performance, its effect on neurological outcomes remains largely unexamined. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a comprehensive multimodal prehabilitation program on cognitive function and fatigue levels in lung cancer patients undergoing elective surgery. Methods: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 77 eligible NSCLC patients were randomized to either a two-week multimodal prehabilitation program (individualized physical exercise, respiratory training, nutritional guidance, and psychological support) or standard preoperative care. Cognitive function was evaluated using Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III), and subjective fatigue was assessed using the Fatigue Assessment Scale (FAS) at baseline (T0), in the early postoperative period (T1), and at two months post-surgery (T2). Between-group differences and longitudinal recovery trajectories were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, and education. Results: Postoperatively, the prehabilitation group achieved significantly higher ACE-III total scores (83.8 ± 9.4 vs. 78.5 ± 10.5; p = 0.049) and language scores (p = 0.015) compared to controls, with total ACE-III benefits maintained at two months (86.8 ± 8.8 vs. 81.9 ± 9.7; p = 0.050). Mixed-effects modeling confirmed significant additional effects of prehabilitation on the recovery trajectories of ACE-III total (β = 3.14, p < 0.001), memory (β = 0.86, p = 0.007), and language (β = 1.19, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the prehabilitation group demonstrated significantly lower total fatigue (β = -5.82, p < 0.001), mental fatigue (β = -2.27, p < 0.001) and physical fatigue (β = -4.31, p < 0.001) immediately following surgery, although fatigue levels converged between cohorts by two months. Conclusions: Comprehensive multimodal prehabilitation significantly attenuates early postoperative cognitive decline, supports cognitive preservation through two months post-surgery, particularly in memory and language, and reduces postoperative fatigue in patients undergoing lung cancer surgery. Trial Registration: ISRCTN15332421 (retrospectively registered on 5 February 2026).

title: From Pleural Drainage to Artificial Intelligence: Selected Historical Milestones and Visionary Pioneers Shaping Innovation in Thoracic Surgery.
authors: Scanagatta P
abstract: Thoracic surgery evolved from procedures aimed at controlling pleural infection and tuberculosis into a technologically advanced specialty integrating oncologic resection, airway and chest wall reconstruction, transplantation, minimally invasive surgery, robotics, and data-driven care. This deliberately selective narrative historical review examines selected turning points that changed the scope or practice of the specialty and the representative pioneers associated with them. A targeted literature search prioritized original landmark reports together with contemporary evidence. The trajectory begins with drainage, collapse therapy, and solutions to open pneumothorax; continues through pneumonectomy, bronchoplastic and sublobar resection, mesothelioma surgery, pulmonary metastasectomy, screening, tracheal reconstruction, lung autotransplantation, and transplantation; and extends to VATS, uniportal and non-intubated surgery, RATS, enhanced recovery, and artificial intelligence. Across these eras, innovation repeatedly shifted from radicality toward preservation and from isolated operative technique toward multidisciplinary perioperative systems. Randomized trials have also shown that progress may require reassessing or abandoning previously accepted surgical paradigms. Thoracic surgery is therefore best understood not as a chronology of operations, but as a continuing process of redefining what is technically possible, oncologically appropriate, physiologically tolerable, and clinically valuable.

title: Segmentectomy or Lobectomy for Early-Stage Lung Cancer? A Patient-Centered Framework for Surgical Decision-Making.
authors: Srivatsa S, Kneuertz PJ
abstract: Randomized trials have established segmentectomy and sublobar resection as oncologically appropriate alternatives to lobectomy for selected patients with small, peripheral, node-negative non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). These findings have expanded surgical options but also shifted the clinical question from whether sublobar resection is adequate to how the extent of resection should be individualized. Patients considering lung cancer surgery want to know: What provides the best chance of cure? How safe is the operation? How will surgery affect breathing and quality of life? What will recovery look like? And which operation is right for them? These questions provide the framework for this review. We examine the evidence needed to address each question, including oncologic outcomes and recurrence, tumor location and achievable margins, lymph node assessment, radiographic and biologic tumor characteristics, perioperative outcomes, preservation of pulmonary function, quality of life, and postoperative recovery. Long-term considerations include competing risks of mortality, the development of second primary lung cancers, and preservation of treatment options for future lung disease. The relative importance of these factors differs among patients and may alter the balance between oncologic control and parenchymal preservation. This review provides a patient-centered framework for integrating tumor characteristics, operative considerations, functional outcomes, and patient factors to individualize the choice between segmentectomy and lobectomy for early-stage NSCLC.

title: Emerging advances in CAR-T therapy for solid tumors: latest clinical trial updates from the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting.
authors: Bao Y, Wang W, Shen H et al.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed the treatment landscape for hematologic malignancies and is under active clinical investigation in solid tumors that are refractory to standard therapies. However, clinical translation in solid tumors remains constrained by intratumoral antigen heterogeneity, limited trafficking and persistence, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and the potential for on-target/off-tumor toxicity and systemic immune-related adverse events. The 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting reported multiple early-phase clinical updates involving autologous and allogeneic CAR-T products for solid tumors. In this focused correspondence, we summarize 12 ASCO 2026 clinical studies reporting extractable efficacy and/or safety outcomes for CAR-T therapy in solid tumors. The included studies encompassed glioblastoma (GBM), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), gastrointestinal cancers, small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC), non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and colorectal peritoneal metastases. The reported strategies included dual-antigen targeting, armored CAR constructs, logic-gated receptors, regional delivery, induced pluripotent stem cell-derived allogeneic products, and mRNA-electroporated autologous CAR-T cells. Across these small, non-randomized early-phase studies, preliminary antitumor activity was observed in selected tumor types and biomarker-defined populations. However, substantial heterogeneity in patient populations, CAR designs, routes of administration, response criteria, follow-up duration, and evaluable populations precludes direct cross-trial efficacy comparisons. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up, standardized biomarker strategies, and comparative trial designs are needed to define the clinical role of CAR-T therapy in solid tumors.

title: Baseline cardiac biomarkers and inflammatory indices for new-onset ECG abnormalities and survival in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors: a single-center exploratory study.
authors: Chen WW, Chen L, Hong G et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine inflammatory and cardiac biomarkers may help risk-stratify patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). The ECG monitoring endpoint and oncologic survival outcomes are distinct. We examined whether baseline cardiac biomarkers were associated with adjudicated new-onset electrocardiographic (ECG) abnormalities after ICI initiation and whether inflammatory and cardiac biomarkers were associated with overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 162 patients with advanced gastrointestinal or lung cancers who received at least two cycles of ICI monotherapy or ICI-based combination therapy. The ECG monitoring endpoint was any adjudicated new-onset ECG abnormality. Baseline ECGs were used to identify pre-existing findings, and ICI initiation was the time origin for the 12-month Cox, Kaplan-Meier, and score analyses. Patients without an event were censored at the earliest of the last evaluable ECG date, death, or 365 days after ICI initiation. ECGs were independently reviewed by two cardiologists, and disagreements were resolved by consensus. Logistic regression and Cox models were used for ECG, OS, and PFS analyses; age-stratified Cox sensitivity analyses addressed non-proportionality.
RESULTS: New-onset ECG abnormalities occurred in 86 patients (53.1%). Study-defined Grade ≥ 2 ECG abnormalities occurred in 25 patients (15.4%). Binary normal/abnormal classification was concordant in all 162 patients, and Cohen's kappa for the specific primary ECG type was 0.975. In the adjusted 12-month Cox model, cTnI > 0.02 ng/mL (HR, 2.00; 95% CI, 1.26-3.18; P = 0.003) and CK-MB > 13 U/L (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.60-4.01; P < 0.001) were associated with shorter time to the first documented adjudicated new-onset ECG abnormality. Age showed non-proportionality, but biomarker estimates were similar in age-stratified sensitivity models. The 3-point score had modest apparent, in-sample discrimination (C-index, 0.645). During follow-up, 53 deaths and 137 PFS events occurred. cTnI remained associated with both OS and PFS after forced adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline cTnI and CK-MB were associated with the first documented adjudicated new-onset ECG abnormality, although discrimination was modest and performance estimates were apparent and in-sample. Separately, cTnI, D-dimer, NLR, and ECOG performance status contributed to exploratory survival risk stratification. ECG abnormalities should not be interpreted as definite ICI-related cardiotoxicity. Prospective multicenter validation is required before these findings can inform clinical monitoring strategies.

title: Economic evaluations of healthcare technologies that incorporate artificial intelligence in radiology: a systematic review.
authors: Espinosa O, Puentes G, Jaimes V et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in radiology has become increasingly relevant due to its potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and optimize healthcare workflows. This study reviews health economic evaluations of AI in radiology, following Cochrane international standards in the field.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies evaluating AI-based health technologies in radiology from a health economics perspective. A qualitative synthesis of the data was performed, and each study was assessed for quality using the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022. The PROSPERO registration number is CRD42024616818.
RESULTS: A total of 938 records were retrieved, with 14 included in the review. Most studies were published between 2021 and 2024. The United States and the United Kingdom had the highest number of studies, with most research focusing on high-income countries. Cost-effectiveness analysis was the most common type of economic evaluation used. X-ray imaging was the most frequently analyzed modality, particularly for cancer detection, with a focus on breast and lung cancer. The most commonly used software for modeling was TreeAge Pro, followed by R and Microsoft Excel.
CONCLUSION: AI in radiology offers substantial clinical benefits, but comprehensive long-term economic evaluations are necessary to fully assess its value. High initial investments, infrastructure changes, and ongoing maintenance were identified as key obstacles, especially in low-resource settings. Future research should prioritize underrepresented regions and incorporate diverse patient demographics to enhance the generalizability of findings.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title: Japan Society of Clinical Oncology Clinical Practice Guidelines 2024 for fertility preservation in childhood, adolescent, and young adult cancer patients: part 3.
authors: Takahashi N, Harada M, Nakayama R et al.
abstract: The Japan Society of Clinical Oncology (JSCO) Clinical Practice Guidelines 2024 for Fertility Preservation in Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult (CAYA) Cancer Patients and Related Diseases include updated guidelines for disease areas in which evidence regarding fertility preservation is often limited. Part 3 of the guideline series describes disease-specific recommendations and explanatory texts for malignant bone and soft tissue tumors, digestive cancers, lung cancer, head and neck cancer, brain tumors, and connective tissue diseases. Background questions, clinical questions, and future questions addressed eligibility for fertility preservation, appropriate timing before cancer or immunosuppressive treatment, pregnancy and childbirth after treatment, use of embryo or oocyte cryopreservation, ovarian tissue cryopreservation, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists, sperm cryopreservation, testicular sperm extraction, nerve-sparing surgery, ovarian transposition, and treatment interruption for pregnancy and childbirth. These recommendations reflect available evidence, clinical urgency, prognosis, treatment-related gonadotoxicity, and feasibility within the Japanese healthcare setting. These guidelines underscore the need to prioritize the treatment of the underlying disease while providing timely information and multidisciplinary support for patients who wish to preserve fertility or consider pregnancy after treatment.

title: Assessment of Engagement and Satisfaction Within a Community Advisory Board to Advance Cancer Prevention and Early Detection Research Among Latinos.
authors: Panizoni E, Orfin R, Ramos-Santiago JW et al.
abstract: Community advisory boards (CABs) are a key component of community-based participatory research, ensuring that community perspectives and priorities are meaningfully integrated into research studies. Despite their recognized importance, assessments of engagement within CABs remain limited. In 2018, we convened a CAB to advance cancer prevention and early detection research among Latinos. The CAB has supported multiple studies across the research continuum, including qualitative, feasibility, efficacy, and dissemination studies. These studies have promoted tobacco cessation and prevention, physical activity, and lung cancer screening. The purpose of this study was to assess engagement and satisfaction within the CAB. Engagement was assessed using the Partnering for Health Improvement and Research Equity scale, and satisfaction was assessed with 2 items evaluating members' experiences with the research team and their willingness to continue working with the CAB. CAB members reported high levels of engagement and satisfaction. Moreover, based on assessment results, CAB members and the research team identified new engagement initiatives, including co-developing infographics summarizing study findings. These findings highlight the value of assessing engagement to understand the dynamics of community-academic partnerships and identify strengths and areas for improvement.

title: From ceremony to cessation: A culturally grounded approach to reducing commercial tobacco use in American Indian communities in North Carolina.
authors: Thoumi A, Raveendran Y, Locklear T et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In North Carolina (NC), over one in four American Indian (AI) adults use commercial tobacco-including cigarettes and e-cigarettes-resulting in disproportionately high smoking-attributable mortality and significantly elevated lung cancer rates compared to non-Hispanic White populations. As part of Southeastern American Indian Cancer health Equity Partnership (SAICEP), we aimed to develop culturally relevant tobacco cessation tools tailored to NC AI communities.
METHODS: Building on previous community-engaged phases of SAICEP that included over 80 community leaders and members, SAICEP partnered with the Duke Smoking Cessation Program (DSCP) to enroll four AI members in an 8-week mindfulness-based cessation program. Participants completed weekly evaluations and participated in a post-training focus group to evaluate DSCP's cultural relevance and inform future adaptations. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify key themes and recommendations.
RESULTS: Participants recommended tailoring cessation programs by dependence severity to ensure relatability and effectiveness. They emphasized distinguishing commercial tobacco use from traditional ceremonial practices to support cultural continuity while promoting cessation. Participants also advocated for incorporating AI imagery, tribal artwork, and culturally relevant design elements, which AI representation on intervention teams could facilitate. Participants proposed co-creating videos featuring respected community members and youth to enhance engagement and motivation. These insights informed the development of a culturally grounded cessation video now being shared across NC AI communities.
CONCLUSIONS: Culturally grounded and tailored smoking cessation strategies are essential for addressing tobacco-related health disparities in AI communities. Honoring traditional values and integrating community voices can enhance program relevance, engagement, and impact.

title: Preoperative Sleep Disturbances, Anxiety, and Depressive Symptoms in Patients with Primary Lung Cancer: Prevalence, Co-Occurrence, and Associated Factors.
authors: Karabul E, Erus S, Cesur E et al.
abstract: Background: Sleep and mood disturbances are common in patients with cancer, but their prevalence, co-occurrence, and associated factors remain insufficiently characterized in patients undergoing surgery for primary lung cancer. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 69 patients with primary lung cancer evaluated before surgery. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) risk was assessed using the Berlin Questionnaire, insomnia using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), restless legs syndrome (RLS) symptoms using a standardized screening questionnaire, anxiety using the Beck Anxiety Inventory, and depressive symptoms using the Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale. Daytime sleepiness and functional outcomes were evaluated using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale and Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with insomnia symptoms. Results: Insomnia symptoms (ISI ≥ 8) were present in 44.9% of patients, including 13.0% with moderate-to-severe insomnia symptoms (ISI ≥ 15). A high OSA screening risk was identified in 33.3%, and RLS symptoms in 21.7%. Moderate-to-severe anxiety symptoms were present in 18.8%, and moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms in 30.9% (21/68). Coexisting insomnia symptoms and a high OSA screening risk were observed in 18.8% of patients. Anxiety scores were higher among patients with insomnia symptoms. In multivariable analysis (n = 68), higher Beck Anxiety Inventory scores were associated with insomnia symptoms after adjustment for age, sex, and depressive symptom severity (adjusted odds ratio 1.12 per point; 95% CI 1.04-1.21; p = 0.004). Among patients with available functional outcome data (n = 60), greater insomnia severity, anxiety symptoms, and daytime sleepiness were associated with poorer sleep-related daytime functioning. Conclusions: Sleep disturbances and psychological symptoms were common before primary lung cancer surgery and frequently co-occurred. Anxiety symptom severity was associated with insomnia symptoms after adjustment for demographic factors and depressive symptom severity. These findings suggest the potential value of integrated preoperative assessment of sleep and psychological symptoms, although further studies are needed to establish its clinical benefits.

title: Prehabilitation Integrated into an Enhanced Recovery Pathway Is Associated with Reduced Cardiopulmonary Complications After Uniportal VATS Lung Resection: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
authors: Salati M, Guiducci GM, Cingolani S et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Postoperative cardiopulmonary complications remain a major source of morbidity after pulmonary resection despite minimally invasive surgery and Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways. We evaluated whether adding a pragmatic prehabilitation program to an established ERAS-based Enhanced Pathway of Care (EPC) was associated with improved outcomes after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) pulmonary resection.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied consecutive adults undergoing uniportal VATS pulmonary resection between May 2019 and April 2024. Patients treated from April 2022 to April 2024 received EPC plus short-term prehabilitation (EPC+PREHAB), whereas those treated from May 2019 to March 2022 received EPC alone. The primary endpoint was postoperative cardiopulmonary complications rate. Secondary endpoints were unplanned intensive care unit (ICU) admission, postoperative length of stay, and 30-day readmission. Propensity score matching was performed 1:1 without replacement using a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score to balance baseline characteristics.
RESULTS: Among 867 eligible patients 435 received EPC+PREHAB and 432 received EPC alone. After propensity score-matched analysis, 345 patients were included in each group. Postoperative cardiopulmonary complications occurred in 77/345 patients (22.3%) in the EPC group and 20/345 (5.8%) in the EPC+PREHAB group (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.13-0.36; p < 0.001). Unplanned ICU admission occurred in five patients (1.4%) in the EPC group and none in the EPC+PREHAB group (p = 0.062). Median postoperative length of stay was 3 days (IQR 3-4) in both groups (p = 0.479), while 30-day readmission occurred in seven patients (2.0%) in each group (p = 1.000). In the anatomical-resection subgroup, cardiopulmonary complications occurred in 30.5% of the EPC group patients versus 6.6% of the EPC+PREHAB group (OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.09-0.31; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Adding a short-term, low-technology prehabilitation program to an established EPC pathway was associated with fewer postoperative cardiopulmonary complications after uniportal VATS pulmonary resection. Prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Surgical and Pathological Outcomes of Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Patients Who Did Not Radiologically Respond to Neoadjuvant Chemo-Immunotherapy.
authors: Suda K, Matsubara T, Ito M et al.
abstract: Background: Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is now a standard treatment for resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with clinical stage II-III disease. However, some patients do not respond to the treatment radiologically, and the surgical and pathological outcomes in such patients remain unclear. Methods: We conducted a multi-institutional retrospective analysis of patients who received neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy at 29 centers in Japan (CReGYT-04 Neo-Venus study). In this study, we focused specifically on radiological non-responders to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy. Results: Of 124 eligible patients, radiological responses indicated a complete/partial response (CR/PR) in 84, stable disease (SD) in 35, and progressive disease (PD) in 5 patients. Nine patients (five with PD, two with SD, and two with PR) did not undergo surgical resection, and one SD patient had exploratory thoracotomy. Surgical outcomes, including minimally invasive approach rates, procedures, operation time, blood loss, and postoperative complications, were similar between patients with SD and those with CR/PR. In the analysis of residual tumor classification, R0 resection was achieved in 88% of patients in the SD group and 98% of those in the CR/PR group. Accordingly, the odds of R1/R2 resection were higher in the SD group than in the CR/PR group (OR, 5.6; 95% CI, 0.8-65.3; p = 0.051). Among 31 SD patients with available pathological data, a major pathologic response (MPR) was achieved in 26%; in an exploratory analysis, pre-treatment PD-L1 status (p < 0.01) and a >50% decrease in the maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax ratio < 50%) on FDG-PET/CT (p = 0.03) were associated with MPR. Conclusions: No statistically significant differences in surgical outcomes, including adverse events, were observed between the SD and CR/PR groups, while the odds of R1/R2 resection were higher in the SD group. Despite the absence of a radiological response, 26% of SD patients achieved MPR, highlighting the limitations of current image-based assessments in evaluating the efficacy of induction chemo-immunotherapy.

title: Comparison of First-Line Pembrolizumab Monotherapy Versus Chemo-Immunotherapy in Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients with PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%: A Multicenter Real-World Study from Turkey.
authors: Celayir ÖM, Köylü B, Muğlu H et al.
abstract: Background and Objectives: This study aimed to compare the real-world outcomes of first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy (Mono-IO) versus pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy (IO + ChT) in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC) and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score (TPS) ≥ 50%. Materials and Methods: This retrospective, multicenter, real-world study evaluated 148 patients with mNSCLC and PD-L1 expression ≥ 50% who received either first-line Mono-IO or IO + ChT. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and clinical benefit rate were compared between the two treatment strategies. Additionally, clinical prognostic factors, patterns of progression, and post-progression treatments were analyzed. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier estimates, multivariable Cox regression, and restricted mean survival time (RMST) analysis. Results: Patients in the Mono-IO group were significantly older (median 69 vs. 63 years; p < 0.001) and had a higher proportion of ECOG PS 2 (35.3% vs. 5.2%; p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between Mono-IO and IO + ChT in median OS (32.0 vs. 26.0 months; p = 0.559) or PFS (19.6 vs. 19.4 months; p = 0.572). In an exploratory multivariable analysis adjusting for organ-specific metastases and antibiotic exposure, ECOG PS ≥ 1 (aHR: 1.86, 95% CI: 1.16-2.97; p = 0.009), antibiotic use (aHR: 1.85, 95% CI: 1.16-2.95; p = 0.010), and liver metastasis (aHR: 2.58, 95% CI: 1.16-5.74; p = 0.020) were independent predictors of worse OS. Conversely, PD-L1 TPS ≥ 90% (aHR: 0.56, 95% CI: 0.35-0.91; p = 0.018) was independently associated with superior OS. In exploratory subgroup analysis, a numerical survival trend favoring Mono-IO was observed in patients with PD-L1 TPS ≥ 90%, although this finding remains hypothesis-generating. Following disease progression, 64.7% of patients received no further systemic therapy. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort, no statistically significant differences in OS or PFS were detected between Mono-IO and IO + ChT; however, the wide confidence intervals do not exclude clinically meaningful differences, and equivalence cannot be inferred from these data. PD-L1 TPS ≥ 90% may potentially serve as a biomarker to identify patients who derive benefit from monotherapy, although this exploratory finding requires validation in larger cohorts. Given that the majority of patients did not transition to subsequent therapy in routine practice, likely reflecting multifactorial host frailty and rapid disease evolution, first-line therapeutic optimization warrants careful individualized consideration.

title: Increased risk of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors in lung cancer: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.
authors: Cheon S, Kim KR, Lee H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have led to a fundamental shift in lung cancer treatment, evidence regarding infections remains limited. Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is a rare but life-threatening opportunistic infection with high mortality if undiagnosed or untreated, making its risk assessment clinically critical. This study aimed to provide population-based comparative evidence on the risk of PJP between ICI therapy and conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy (CC) in patients with lung cancer.
METHODS: Using the Korean nationwide claims data, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients newly diagnosed with lung cancer who initiated CC or ICI therapy between 2017 and 2022. After propensity score matching, incidence rate ratios (IRRs), Cox hazard ratios (HRs), and Fine-Gray subdistribution HRs (sHRs) were estimated. Sensitivity analyses were performed across clinically relevant subgroups, including those defined by advanced stage, surgical resection, radiotherapy, treatment line, ICI monotherapy, and systemic corticosteroid use. Additionally, risk patterns across specific ICI agents, including atezolizumab, pembrolizumab, durvalumab, and nivolumab, were evaluated in an exploratory analysis.
RESULTS: After matching, 13,426 patients were included in each group. During follow-up, 27 and 66 PJP events occurred in the CC and ICI groups, respectively, corresponding to IRs of 3.35 and 7.77 per 1,000 person-years. ICI therapy was associated with a significantly higher risk of PJP (adjusted IRR 2.26, 95% CI 1.46-3.59; adjusted HR 2.83, 95% CI 1.81-4.44; adjusted sHR 2.63, 95% CI 1.68-4.12). In the exploratory analysis, significantly elevated IRRs, HRs, and sHRs were observed for durvalumab, pembrolizumab, and atezolizumab, while no clear association was observed for nivolumab because of the limited number of events. This association remained robust and consistent across various clinical contexts including cohorts defined by disease stage, treatment line, the use of monotherapy, and patients without systemic steroid exposure.
CONCLUSIONS: ICI therapy is associated with a significantly increased risk of PJP compared with CC in patients with lung cancer. Given the potential severity of PJP, enhanced clinical vigilance is warranted during ICI treatment.
